chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed Al-Nowfaly, from Ismail ibn Abu Ziyad Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not cut off the question of the beggar; if it were not for the fact that the poor lie, the one who repels them would not prosper.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on dismissing beggars who might be lying?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the Prophet’s instruction to avoid abruptly dismissing beggars, highlighting that even if the poor are deceitful, repelling them leads to spiritual failure. This teaching underscores the virtue of patience and generosity in social interactions, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining dignity and compassion towards the needy regardless of their truthfulness.
